source.text: כִּ֤י יְבִֽיאֲךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ וְנָשַׁ֣ל גּֽוֹיִם־רַבִּ֣ים׀מִפָּנֶ֡יךָ הַֽחִתִּי֩ וְהַגִּרְגָּשִׁ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַכְּנַעֲנִ֣י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֗י וְהַֽחִוִּי֙ וְהַיְבוּסִ֔י שִׁבְעָ֣ה גוֹיִ֔ם רַבִּ֥ים וַעֲצוּמִ֖ים מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: When brings you Yahweh your God into the land which you [are] going there to possess it, and clears away nations many from before you, the Hittite[s] and the Girgashite[s] and the Amorite[s] and the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s], seven nations many and mighty more than you,

en.L: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brings you into the land which you are going into to take possession of it, and clears away many nations before you, the Hittite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, seven nations more numerous and mightier than you,
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brings you into the land you are about to enter and take as your own, and clears many nations out of your way, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, seven nations greater in number and might than you,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land you are going to take over. He will force many nations out of your way: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. There are seven of them, and they are bigger and stronger than you.

es.L: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te introduzca en la tierra adonde tú vas para tomar posesión de ella, y aparte de delante de ti muchas naciones, al hitita y al gergeseo y al amorreo y al cananeo y al ferezeo y al heveo y al jebuseo, siete naciones más numerosas y más poderosas que tú,
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te lleve a la tierra donde estás a punto de entrar para tomar posesión de ella, y quite de tu camino a muchas naciones, a los hititas, gergeseos, amorreos, cananeos, ferezeos, heveos y jebuseos, siete naciones más numerosas y más fuertes que tú,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te llevará a la tierra que vas a tomar como tuya. Echará de tu camino a muchas naciones: los hititas, gergeseos, amorreos, cananeos, ferezeos, heveos y jebuseos. Son siete naciones, y son más grandes y más fuertes que tú.

fr.L: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te fera entrer dans le pays où tu vas pour en prendre possession, et écartera devant toi des nations nombreuses, le Hittite et le Guirgasien et l’Amoréen et le Cananéen et le Phérézien et l’Hévien et le Jébusien, sept nations plus nombreuses et plus puissantes que toi,
fr.B: Lorsque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’aura fait entrer dans le pays dont tu vas prendre possession, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aura écarté de ton chemin de nombreuses nations, les Hittites, les Guirgasiens, les Amoréens, les Cananéens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens, sept nations plus nombreuses et plus fortes que toi,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va te faire entrer dans le pays que tu vas prendre. Il va chasser de ton chemin beaucoup de nations : les Hittites, les Guirgasiens, les Amoréens, les Cananéens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens. Ce sont sept nations plus grandes et plus fortes que toi.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuingiza katika nchi unayoiendea ili kuimiliki, na kuyaondoa mataifa mengi mbele yako, Mhiti na Mgirgashi na Mwamori na Mkanaani na Mperizi na Mhivi na Myebusi, mataifa saba, mengi na yenye nguvu kuliko wewe,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuingiza katika nchi unayokwenda kuimiliki, na kuyaondoa mataifa mengi njiani mwako, yaani Wahiti, Wagirgashi, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi, mataifa saba yaliyo mengi na yenye nguvu kuliko wewe,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakuingiza katika nchi utakayoichukua iwe yako. Atayafukuza mataifa mengi kutoka njia yako: Wahiti, Wagirgashi, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi. Ni mataifa saba, nayo ni makubwa na yenye nguvu kuliko wewe.

decisions.choice: Moses is still speaking: the address begun at 5:1 runs on
decisions.reason: No new speaker is introduced here, and no quotation opens or closes. Moses' address that began at 5:1 continues to 26:19. Chapters 5-11 lay down the heart of the covenant, loyalty to the LORD alone, before the laws of chapters 12-26; in this chapter Moses turns to how Israel is to deal with the peoples of the land and their gods.

decisions.choice: clears away: removes, as something slipping off
decisions.reason: The verb means to slip off or pull away, as a sandal comes off the foot (Exodus 3:5) or an axe head flies off its handle (19:5). God will remove the nations from Israel's path. The same verb returns in verse 22, where he does it little by little.

decisions.choice: seven nations: the peoples living in Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: Lists of the peoples of the land appear in several forms (Genesis 15:19-21; Exodus 3:8; 23:23; 34:11). This one has seven names and includes the Girgashites, who are missing from the Exodus lists; seven stands for the whole of the land's population. Each name is singular in the Hebrew, standing for a whole people.

decisions.choice: you: Israel addressed as one person, and at times as many
decisions.reason: Moses speaks to Israel as "you" in the singular, the nation as one person. In places he moves to the plural (verses 4-5, 7-8, 12), speaking to the people as a body of many. The two forms address the same people and do not change the sense.

decisions.choice: Hittites, Girgashites ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural names for the peoples, as Exodus 34:11 does; Literal keeps the singular of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: will bring you ... He will force
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long "when" clause into plain statements; verse 2 picks up with what Israel is then to do.

decisions.choice: "tú" for Israel addressed in the singular ("tu Dios", "te"), with the plural_you span only where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verses 4-5, 7-8, 12, 25)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1, Spanish follows the Hebrew number of "you" at every level, since Spanish, unlike English, can show it.

decisions.choice: "tu" for Israel addressed in the singular, "vous" where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verses 4-5, 7-8, 12, 25)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1, French follows the Hebrew number of "you" at every level, since French, unlike English, can show it.

decisions.choice: singular forms ("wewe", "Mungu wako") for Israel addressed as one, plural forms ("ninyi", "-enu") where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verses 4-5, 7-8, 12, 25)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1, Swahili follows the Hebrew number of "you" at every level, since Swahili, unlike English, can show it.

source.text: וּנְתָנָ֞ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ לְפָנֶ֖יךָ וְהִכִּיתָ֑ם הַחֲרֵ֤ם תַּחֲרִים֙ אֹתָ֔ם לֹא־תִכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם בְּרִ֖ית וְלֹ֥א תְחָנֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and gives them Yahweh your God before you, and you strike them, devoting to destruction you shall devote them to destruction; not you shall make with them a covenant, and not you shall show them favor.

en.L: and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gives them [over] before you, and you strike them, you shall utterly devote them to destruction. You shall not make a covenant with them, and you shall not show them favor.
en.B: and when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, then you are to devote them wholly to destruction. Make no covenant with them, and grant them no favor.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hands them over to you and you defeat them, you must destroy them completely, as people given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Do not make any agreement with them, and do not spare them.

es.L: y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios las entregue delante de ti, y tú las derrotes, las consagrarás por completo a la destrucción. No harás pacto con ellas, y no les mostrarás favor.
es.B: y cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te las entregue y las derrotes, entonces deberás consagrarlas por completo a la destrucción. No hagas pacto con ellas ni les concedas ningún favor.
es.R: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te las entregue y las derrotes, tendrás que destruirlas por completo, como pueblos entregados {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. No hagas ningún acuerdo con ellas, y no les perdones la vida.

fr.L: et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu les livrera devant toi, et que tu les frapperas, tu les voueras entièrement à la destruction. Tu ne concluras pas d’alliance avec elles, et tu ne leur feras pas grâce.
fr.B: et lorsque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te les aura livrées et que tu les auras battues, alors tu les voueras entièrement à la destruction. Ne conclus pas d’alliance avec elles et ne leur accorde aucune grâce.
fr.R: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te les livrera et que tu les vaincras, tu devras les détruire complètement, comme des nations données {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Ne fais aucun accord avec elles, et ne les épargne pas.

sw.L: na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapowatoa mbele yako, nawe ukawapiga, hakika utawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi. Usifanye agano nao, wala usiwafanyie fadhili.
sw.B: na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapowatia mikononi mwako nawe ukawashinda, basi utawaweka wakfu kabisa kwa maangamizi. Usifanye agano nao, wala usiwaonyeshe fadhili yoyote.
sw.R: Atakapowatia mikononi mwako na ukawashinda, lazima uwaangamize kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Usifanye mapatano yoyote nao, na usiwahurumie.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over wholly to the LORD by destroying
decisions.reason: The verb is the one behind the "devoted thing" of Leviticus 27:28-29: something taken out of human use and handed over to the LORD for good, never to be bought back. In war it means that the enemy is destroyed and nothing is kept for private gain (Numbers 21:2-3; Deuteronomy 2:34; 20:16-18; Joshua 6:17-19). The verb is doubled for emphasis: completely, with nothing held back.

decisions.choice: the ban on the peoples of the land: a judgment bound to this land and its worship
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest commands in Scripture, and Deuteronomy itself gives its limits and its reasons. It applies only to the peoples living in the land Israel was entering; towns far away were first to be offered peace (20:10-18). The reason given is worship: these peoples would turn Israel to serve other gods (verse 4; 12:29-31; 20:18). The wrongs of the land's people are named as the ground of God's judgment on them, not Israel's own goodness (9:4-5; Genesis 15:16; Leviticus 18:24-25). The same ban falls on an Israelite town that turns to other gods (13:13-19), and on any Israelite who takes what is devoted (verse 26; Joshua 7). The commands around it, not to marry these peoples (verse 3) and to clear them away little by little (verse 22), assume that they will still be present for some time, and the later accounts tell of people of the land who were spared, such as Rahab's family and the Gibeonites (Joshua 6:25; 9). The verse states the command as it was given; it does not by itself settle how fully it was carried out or how its strong language of war is to be weighed.

decisions.choice: show them favor: be gracious to them, spare them
decisions.reason: The verb means to be gracious or to show kindness that is not owed. Beside "make no covenant" it rules out granting these peoples terms of peace or sparing them; verse 16 says the same with another picture ("your eye shall not pity them").

decisions.choice: gives them before you: puts them in your power
decisions.reason: To "give" an enemy "before" someone is to hand them over in battle (1:8; 2:31, 33). The victory is the LORD's gift; Israel's striking follows from it.

decisions.choice: destroy them completely, as people given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words, as Numbers 21:2 does: the peoples are to be destroyed because they are given over to the LORD, not taken for gain. Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction".

decisions.choice: agreement; do not spare them
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:12, Readable says "agreement" for a covenant between peoples; Literal and Balanced keep "covenant". "Do not spare them" gives the sense of "show them no favor" in this setting (m3).

source.text: וְלֹ֥א תִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בָּ֑ם בִּתְּךָ֙ לֹא־תִתֵּ֣ן לִבְנ֔וֹ וּבִתּ֖וֹ לֹא־תִקַּ֥ח לִבְנֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not you shall make marriages with them; your daughter not you shall give to his son, and his daughter not you shall take for your son.

en.L: And you shall not make marriages with them: your daughter you shall not give to his son, and his daughter you shall not take for your son.
en.B: Do not join your families to theirs by marriage: your daughters are not to marry their sons, nor are your sons to take their daughters as wives.
en.R: Do not let your families marry into theirs. Do not let your daughters marry their sons, or your sons marry their daughters.

es.L: Y no contraerás matrimonios con ellas: a tu hija no la darás a su hijo, y a su hija no la tomarás para tu hijo.
es.B: No emparentes con ellos por matrimonio: tus hijas no se casarán con sus hijos, ni tus hijos tomarán por esposas a sus hijas.
es.R: No dejes que tu familia se una a la de ellos por casamiento. No permitas que tus hijas se casen con sus hijos, ni que tus hijos se casen con sus hijas.

fr.L: Et tu ne t’allieras pas par mariage avec elles : ta fille, tu ne la donneras pas à son fils, et sa fille, tu ne la prendras pas pour ton fils.
fr.B: Ne t’unis pas à eux par des mariages : tes filles ne doivent pas épouser leurs fils, et tes fils ne doivent pas prendre leurs filles pour femmes.
fr.R: Ne laisse pas ta famille s’unir à la leur par le mariage. Ne laisse pas tes filles épouser leurs fils, ni tes fils épouser leurs filles.

sw.L: Wala usioane nao: binti yako usimpe mwana wake, wala binti yake usimtwae kwa ajili ya mwana wako.
sw.B: Usiziunganishe familia zako na zao kwa ndoa: binti zako wasiolewe na wana wao, wala wana wako wasioe binti zao.
sw.R: Usikubali familia yako ioane na familia zao. Usiwaruhusu binti zako waolewe na wana wao, wala wana wako waoe binti zao.

decisions.choice: make marriages: become related by marriage
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the words for a father-in-law and a son-in-law. It means to join two families by marriage, which in that world also made an alliance between them (Genesis 34:9; Joshua 23:12; 1 Kings 3:1).

decisions.choice: your daughter, his son: each family, on either side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of one daughter and one son, and "his" refers to a man of those peoples. The command covers every such marriage, either way round.

decisions.choice: daughters, sons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plurals, since the command covers every family (m2); Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: כִּֽי־יָסִ֤יר אֶת־בִּנְךָ֙ מֵֽאַחֲרַ֔י וְעָבְד֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְחָרָ֤ה אַף־יְהוָה֙ בָּכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁמִידְךָ֖ מַהֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: For he will turn your son from after me, and they will serve gods other; and will burn [the] anger of Yahweh against you, and he will destroy you quickly.

en.L: For he will turn your son away from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they will serve other gods; then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will burn against you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy you quickly.
en.B: For they would draw your sons away from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, into the service of other gods, and then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would flare up against you and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would soon destroy you.
en.R: They would turn your sons away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to worship other gods. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would be very angry with you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would soon destroy you.

es.L: Porque apartará a tu hijo de en pos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y servirán a otros dioses; y se encenderá la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y te destruirá pronto.
es.B: Porque ellos apartarían a tus hijos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para servir a otros dioses, y entonces la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se encendería contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y te destruiría en poco tiempo.
es.R: Ellos harían que tus hijos se apartaran de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para adorar a otros dioses. Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojaría mucho con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y te destruiría pronto.

fr.L: Car il détournera ton fils de [marcher] derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils serviront d’autres dieux ; et la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflammera contre vous, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te détruira promptement.
fr.B: Car ils détourneraient tes fils de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivre, pour servir d’autres dieux ; alors la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’enflammerait contre vous, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aurait vite fait de te détruire.
fr.R: Ils pousseraient tes fils à se détourner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} pour adorer d’autres dieux. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} serait très en colère contre vous, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te détruirait vite.

sw.L: Kwa maana atamgeuza mwana wako asinifuate {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, nao watatumikia miungu mingine; na hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} itawaka juu yenu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakuangamiza upesi.
sw.B: Kwa maana wangewageuza wana wako waache kunifuata {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na kutumikia miungu mingine, na hapo hasira ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ingewaka juu yenu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} angekuangamiza upesi.
sw.R: Wangewafanya wana wako waniache {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ili kuabudu miungu mingine. Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} angewakasirikia sana, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} angekuangamiza upesi.

decisions.choice: following me: Moses speaks in God's own voice
decisions.reason: The "me" is the LORD. Moses moves from speaking about God to speaking as God, as a prophet does, without a word to mark the change (compare 11:13-15; 29:4-5). The same sentence then speaks of "the anger of the LORD" in the third person.

decisions.choice: he will turn: the foreign in-law, or that people as a whole
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. It most likely refers to the man of verse 3 whose daughter is married into an Israelite family, or to the foreign people taken as one. "Your son" is the Israelite who marries into them; "they will serve" is plural, because the turning spreads. The warning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the anger of the LORD will burn: he will become fiercely angry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for anger is the nose, which grows hot with rage (6:15; 11:17; Exodus 32:10).

decisions.choice: they would turn your sons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plurals to match verse 3, and "would", since this is what would happen if the marriages of verse 3 were made. Literal keeps the Hebrew's singular and plain future.

source.text: כִּֽי־אִם־כֹּ֤ה תַעֲשׂוּ֙ לָהֶ֔ם מִזְבְּחֹתֵיהֶ֣ם תִּתֹּ֔צוּ וּמַצֵּבֹתָ֖ם תְּשַׁבֵּ֑רוּ וַאֲשֵֽׁירֵהֶם֙ תְּגַדֵּע֔וּן וּפְסִילֵיהֶ֖ם תִּשְׂרְפ֥וּן בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: But rather thus you shall do to them: their altars you shall tear down, and their pillars you shall break, and their Asherah [poles] you shall cut down, and their carved images you shall burn with fire.

en.L: But this is what you shall do to them: their altars you shall tear down, and their pillars you shall break, and their Asherah poles you shall cut down, and their carved images you shall burn with fire.
en.B: Instead, deal with them in this way: pull down their altars, break their standing stones to pieces, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images.
en.R: Instead, this is what you must do to them. Tear down their altars. Break their stone pillars used in worship. Cut down the wooden poles they use to worship the goddess Asherah. Burn up their idols.

es.L: Sino que así {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} con ellos: sus altares {{plural_you:derribarán|derribaréis}}, y sus estelas {{plural_you:quebrarán|quebraréis}}, y sus postes de Aserá {{plural_you:cortarán|cortaréis}}, y sus imágenes talladas {{plural_you:quemarán|quemaréis}} en el fuego.
es.B: Al contrario, {{plural_you:trátenlos|tratadlos}} de esta manera: {{plural_you:derriben|derribad}} sus altares, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} pedazos sus piedras sagradas, {{plural_you:corten|cortad}} sus postes de Aserá y {{plural_you:quemen|quemad}} sus imágenes talladas.
es.R: Al contrario, esto es lo que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer con ellos. {{plural_you:Derriben|Derribad}} sus altares. {{plural_you:Rompan|Romped}} las piedras que levantan para adorar a sus dioses. {{plural_you:Corten|Cortad}} los postes de madera que usan para adorar a la diosa Aserá. {{plural_you:Quemen|Quemad}} sus ídolos.

fr.L: Mais voici comment vous agirez envers eux : leurs autels, vous les démolirez, et leurs stèles, vous les briserez, et leurs poteaux d’Ashéra, vous les abattrez, et leurs images taillées, vous les brûlerez au feu.
fr.B: Au contraire, voici ce que vous leur ferez : démolissez leurs autels, mettez en pièces leurs pierres dressées, abattez leurs poteaux d’Ashéra et brûlez leurs idoles sculptées.
fr.R: Voici plutôt ce que vous devez faire. Démolissez leurs autels. Cassez les pierres qu’ils dressent pour leur culte. Coupez les poteaux de bois qu’ils utilisent pour adorer la déesse Ashéra. Brûlez leurs idoles.

sw.L: Bali hivi ndivyo mtakavyowatendea: madhabahu zao mtazibomoa, na nguzo zao mtazivunja, na miti yao ya Ashera mtaikata, na sanamu zao za kuchonga mtaziteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: Badala yake, watendeeni hivi: bomoeni madhabahu zao, vunjeni vipande vipande nguzo zao za mawe, kateni miti yao ya Ashera, na chomeni kwa moto sanamu zao za kuchonga.
sw.R: Badala yake, hivi ndivyo mnavyopaswa kuwatendea. Bomoeni madhabahu zao. Vunjeni nguzo za mawe wanazotumia katika ibada. Kateni nguzo za miti wanazotumia kumwabudu mungu wa kike Ashera. Chomeni sanamu zao.

decisions.choice: but rather: instead of covenant or marriage
decisions.reason: The opening words set this against verses 2-3: rather than making ties with these peoples, Israel is to destroy their places and objects of worship. The command is repeated in 12:3. Moses here speaks to the people in the plural (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up in worship
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:13: upright stones that stood at places of worship. The Canaanite ones belonged to their gods and were to be broken (12:3; 16:22).

decisions.choice: Asherah poles: wooden objects for the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:13. Asherah was a Canaanite goddess whose symbol was a wooden pole or tree beside an altar; it could be cut down and burned (12:3; Judges 6:25-26).

decisions.choice: carved images: idols cut from wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to cut or carve. Such images were often covered with silver or gold (verse 25). The second commandment forbids making them (5:8).

decisions.choice: standing stones; stone pillars used in worship; wooden poles ... Asherah
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:13: Balanced and Readable say what the pillars were, and Readable explains the name Asherah. Literal keeps "pillars".

decisions.choice: "poteaux d'Ashéra"
decisions.reason: The name stays, as in the English, with "poteaux" saying what the objects were; Readable explains the goddess as the English does.

decisions.choice: "miti ya Ashera"
decisions.reason: "Miti" (wooden posts, trees) keeps the Asherah objects apart from the standing stones, which are "nguzo" in the same verse.

source.text: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּךָ֞ בָּחַ֣ר׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ לִהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה מִכֹּל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For a people holy [are] you to Yahweh your God; you has chosen Yahweh your God to be for him a people [of] treasured possession out of all the peoples which [are] on [the] face of the ground.

en.L: For you [are] a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has chosen you to be a people of treasured possession for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of all the peoples who [are] on the face of the ground.
en.B: You are a people set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. From among every people on the face of the earth, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God picked you out to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} treasured possession.
en.R: You are a holy people, set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Out of all the peoples on earth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own treasure.

es.L: Porque pueblo santo [eres] tú para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios; a ti te ha escogido {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios para que seas para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} un pueblo de posesión preciada entre todos los pueblos que [están] sobre la faz de la tierra.
es.B: Tú eres un pueblo consagrado como santo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios. De entre todos los pueblos que hay sobre la faz de la tierra, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te escogió para que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pertenezcas como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} tesoro personal.
es.R: Tú eres un pueblo santo, apartado para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. De entre todos los pueblos de la tierra, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te escogió para que seas {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio tesoro.

fr.L: Car tu [es] un peuple saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a choisi pour être pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un peuple, un trésor particulier, parmi tous les peuples qui [sont] sur la face du sol.
fr.B: Tu es un peuple mis à part, saint pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Parmi tous les peuples qui sont sur la face de la terre, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a choisi pour que tu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartiennes comme {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre trésor.
fr.R: Tu es un peuple saint, mis à part pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Parmi tous les peuples de la terre, c’est toi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi pour être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trésor à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana wewe [ni] taifa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako; {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekuchagua uwe {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} taifa la milki ya pekee kutoka katika mataifa yote yaliyo juu ya uso wa ardhi.
sw.B: Wewe ni taifa lililotengwa kuwa takatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Kati ya mataifa yote yaliyo juu ya uso wa dunia, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alikuchagua uwe mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, hazina {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pekee.
sw.R: Wewe ni taifa takatifu, lililotengwa kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Kati ya mataifa yote duniani, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuchagua uwe hazina {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pekee.

decisions.choice: holy: set apart, belonging to the LORD
decisions.reason: To be holy is to be set apart for God and to belong to him. This is why Israel must have nothing to do with the worship of the nations (verse 5). The same words return in 14:2, 21 and 26:19, and echo Exodus 19:6.

decisions.choice: treasured possession: a personal treasure
decisions.reason: The word means property that is one's own in a special way, such as a king's private treasure (1 Chronicles 29:3; Ecclesiastes 2:8). God first called Israel this at Sinai (Exodus 19:5); it returns in 14:2 and 26:18.

decisions.choice: chosen: picked out by God's own decision
decisions.reason: The verb of choosing is a key word in Deuteronomy for God's choice of Israel (4:37; 10:15; 14:2) and of the place where he will be worshiped (12:5). Verses 7-8 say why he chose.

decisions.choice: earth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "ground" or "soil"; "the face of the ground" means the whole inhabited earth. Literal keeps "ground".

source.text: לֹ֣א מֵֽרֻבְּכֶ֞ם מִכָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֗ים חָשַׁ֧ק יְהוָ֛ה בָּכֶ֖ם וַיִּבְחַ֣ר בָּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֥ם הַמְעַ֖ט מִכָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Not because of your being more than all the peoples did set his love Yahweh on you and choose you, for you [were] the fewest of all the peoples,

en.L: Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love on you and choose you, for you [were] the fewest of all the peoples,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart to you and chose you, not because there were more of you than of any other people, for you were the smallest of all the peoples,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did not love you and choose you because you were a bigger nation than others. You were the smallest nation of all.

es.L: No porque {{plural_you:ustedes fueran|vosotros fuerais}} más numerosos que todos los pueblos puso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} escogió, pues {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [{{plural_you:eran|erais}}] los menos numerosos de todos los pueblos,
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} escogió, no porque {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} más numerosos que cualquier otro pueblo, pues {{plural_you:eran|erais}} el más pequeño de todos los pueblos,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no {{plural_you:los|os}} amó ni {{plural_you:los|os}} escogió porque {{plural_you:fueran|fuerais}} una nación más grande que las demás. {{plural_you:Ustedes eran|Vosotros erais}} la nación más pequeña de todas.

fr.L: Ce n’est pas parce que vous étiez plus nombreux que tous les peuples que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a mis {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour en vous et vous a choisis, car vous [étiez] les moins nombreux de tous les peuples,
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est attaché à vous de tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} cœur et vous a choisis, non parce que vous étiez plus nombreux que tout autre peuple, car vous étiez le plus petit de tous les peuples,
fr.R: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a aimés et vous a choisis, ce n’est pas parce que vous étiez une nation plus grande que les autres. Vous étiez la plus petite de toutes les nations.

sw.L: Si kwa sababu mlikuwa wengi kuliko mataifa yote ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaweka upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwenu na kuwachagua, kwa maana ninyi [mlikuwa] wachache kuliko mataifa yote,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapenda kwa moyo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote na kuwachagua, si kwa sababu mlikuwa wengi kuliko taifa lingine lolote, kwa maana mlikuwa wadogo kuliko mataifa yote,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwapenda na kuwachagua kwa sababu mlikuwa taifa kubwa kuliko mengine. Ninyi mlikuwa taifa dogo kuliko yote.

decisions.choice: set his love: be bound to someone in love and desire
decisions.reason: The verb describes love that attaches itself to someone, as Shechem's love for Dinah (Genesis 34:8). Deuteronomy uses it for God's love for Israel's ancestors (10:15). It is a love freely given, as verse 8 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: the fewest: the smallest in number
decisions.reason: Israel began as a family of seventy who went down to Egypt (10:22; 26:5). Elsewhere Moses says they have become as many as the stars (1:10), but that growth was the LORD's blessing, not the reason he chose them.

decisions.choice: give his heart to you
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English phrase for love that fixes itself on someone, to show that this verb is stronger than the ordinary word for love in verse 8.

source.text: כִּי֩ מֵֽאַהֲבַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה אֶתְכֶ֗ם וּמִשָּׁמְר֤וּאֶת־הַשְּׁבֻעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁבַּע֙ לַאֲבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם הוֹצִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֑ה וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים מִיַּ֖ד פַּרְעֹ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: but because of Yahweh's loving you and because of his keeping the oath which he swore to your fathers, brought out Yahweh you with a hand strong and redeemed you from [the] house of slaves, from [the] hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

en.L: but because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s loving you and because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} keeping the oath which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
en.B: but because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loved you and would not break the oath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your ancestors. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led you out by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strong hand and bought you free from the house where you were slaves, out of the grip of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loved you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made to your ancestors with an oath. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring you out. He set you free from slavery under Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.

es.L: sino porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ama, y porque guarda el juramento que juró a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} sacó con mano fuerte y te rescató de la casa de esclavos, de la mano del faraón, rey de Egipto.
es.B: sino porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} amaba y no quería romper el juramento que había hecho a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}. Por eso {{plural_you:los|os}} sacó con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano poderosa y te compró la libertad, librándote de la casa donde eras esclavo, de las garras del faraón, rey de Egipto.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:los|os}} amaba, y cumplió la promesa que había hecho con juramento a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}. Por eso usó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran poder para {{plural_you:sacarlos|sacaros}} de allí. Te libró de la esclavitud bajo el faraón, rey de Egipto.

fr.L: mais parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous aime, et parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} garde le serment qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a juré à vos pères, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a fait sortir à main forte et t’a racheté de la maison des esclaves, de la main de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte.
fr.B: mais parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous aimait et ne voulait pas rompre le serment qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait à vos ancêtres. C’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a fait sortir par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main puissante et t’a racheté pour te rendre libre, hors de la maison où tu étais esclave, hors des griffes de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a aimés, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a tenu la promesse qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait faite avec serment à vos ancêtres. C’est pour cela qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a utilisé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grande puissance pour vous faire sortir. Il t’a libéré de l’esclavage sous Pharaon, le roi d’Égypte.

sw.L: bali kwa sababu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuwapenda, na kwa sababu ya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kukishika kiapo alichowaapia baba zenu, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatoa kwa mkono hodari, akakukomboa kutoka nyumba ya watumwa, kutoka mkononi mwa Farao mfalme wa Misri.
sw.B: bali kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapenda, na hakutaka kukivunja kiapo alichowaapia mababu zenu. Kwa hiyo aliwatoa kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wenye nguvu, akakukomboa ukawa huru kutoka nyumba ambamo ulikuwa mtumwa, kutoka mikononi mwa Farao mfalme wa Misri.
sw.R: Lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapenda, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alitimiza ahadi aliyowaahidi mababu zenu kwa kiapo. Ndiyo sababu alitumia nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kuu kuwatoa huko. Alikuweka huru kutoka utumwani chini ya Farao, mfalme wa Misri.

decisions.choice: because the LORD loves you: his choice rests on his own love and promise
decisions.reason: Verses 7-8 give no reason in Israel itself for God's choice: not their size, and elsewhere not their goodness (9:4-6). The only reasons are his love and his faithfulness to his oath (4:37; 10:15).

decisions.choice: the oath he swore to your fathers: the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: God swore to give the land to the patriarchs and their descendants (Genesis 22:16-18; 26:3; Deuteronomy 1:8; 6:10).

decisions.choice: a strong hand: God's power at work
decisions.reason: The hand stands for strength and action. The phrase recalls the rescue from Egypt (4:34; 5:15; Exodus 13:9).

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free by paying or acting for someone
decisions.reason: The verb is used for buying a person or animal free (Exodus 13:13-15). Here God frees Israel from slavery, as if paying the price himself (13:6; 15:15; 24:18). "The house of slaves" pictures Egypt as a household of slaves (5:6; Exodus 20:2).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forefathers, the patriarchs; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors". Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: slaves, slavery
decisions.reason: "Slaves" stays at every level for Israel's slavery in Egypt, as the style guide keeps it (Exodus 20:2).

decisions.choice: bought you free; out of the grip of
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "redeemed" means (m4), and "the hand of Pharaoh" is his power over Israel. Literal keeps "redeemed" and "the hand of".

decisions.choice: So; That is why
decisions.reason: Readable (and Balanced, with "So") makes two sentences and links them, so that it stays clear that God's love and oath are the reason he brought Israel out.

decisions.choice: plural "los sacó", then singular "te rescató" / "te libró"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brought you (plural) out" and "redeemed you (singular)" in one sentence; Spanish keeps the change, as the chapter follows the Hebrew number.

decisions.choice: "vous a fait sortir", then "t'a racheté" / "t'a libéré"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brought you (plural) out" and "redeemed you (singular)" in one sentence; French keeps the change, as the chapter follows the Hebrew number.

decisions.choice: "aliwatoa" (plural), then "akakukomboa" / "alikuweka huru" (singular)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brought you (plural) out" and "redeemed you (singular)" in one sentence; Swahili keeps the change, as the chapter follows the Hebrew number.

source.text: וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ ה֣וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים הָאֵל֙ הַֽנֶּאֱמָ֔ן שֹׁמֵ֧ר הַבְּרִ֣ית וְהַחֶ֗סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֛יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָ֖יו לְאֶ֥לֶף דּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you shall know that Yahweh your God, he [is] the God, the God the faithful, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love for those loving him and for those keeping his commandments, to a thousand generation[s],

en.L: Know therefore that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the God, the faithful God, keeping the covenant and the steadfast love for those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for those who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, to a thousand generations,
en.B: So understand that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the true God, the faithful God. He keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love for a thousand generations with those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,
en.R: So you must know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one true God. He is a God you can trust. He keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and shows faithful love to those who love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. He does this for a thousand generations.

decisions.choice: he is the God: the one who truly is God
decisions.reason: With the article, "the God" means the God there really is, with no other beside him, as in 4:35 and 4:39. Israel is to know this and live by it.

decisions.choice: faithful: reliable, true to his word
decisions.reason: The word means firm and dependable, one who can be relied on to keep a promise (32:4; Isaiah 49:7).

decisions.choice: the covenant and the steadfast love: loyal love that keeps the covenant
decisions.reason: The two words go together: God keeps his covenant and the loyal, faithful love that belongs to it (verse 12; 1 Kings 8:23). The word for steadfast love is the one in Exodus 20:6 and 34:6.

decisions.choice: those who love him ... to a thousand generations: the words of the second commandment
decisions.reason: The phrase takes up 5:9-10 (Exodus 20:5-6), where God shows love "to thousands". Here it is spelled out as a thousand generations. Loving God and keeping his commandments go together (6:5-6; 11:1).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:6 and 34:6, so that the loyalty in the word is kept.

decisions.choice: the true God; a God you can trust
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the God" means (m1); Readable says "faithful" in plain words. Literal keeps "the God".

source.text: וּמְשַׁלֵּ֧ם לְשֹׂנְאָ֛יו אֶל־פָּנָ֖יו לְהַאֲבִיד֑וֹ לֹ֤א יְאַחֵר֙ לְשֹׂ֣נְא֔וֹ אֶל־פָּנָ֖יו יְשַׁלֶּם־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and repaying those hating him to his face, to destroy him; not he will delay with the one hating him; to his face he will repay him.

en.L: and repaying those who hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to [each one's] face, to destroy him. He will not delay with the one who hates {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; to his face {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay him.
en.B: but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repays those who hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, each one in person, and destroys them. He does not put off dealing with anyone who hates {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repays that person directly.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pays back each person who hates {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and destroys them. He does not wait. He pays back the very person who hates {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: to his face: directly, the person himself
decisions.reason: "To the face" of someone means to that person himself, openly. The one who hates God is repaid in person, not only through those who come after him. The verse sets this beside verse 9: God's love reaches a thousand generations, while his judgment falls on those who hate him.

decisions.choice: repay: pay back what is due
decisions.reason: The verb means to make complete, and so to pay what is owed, whether reward or punishment (32:35, 41).

decisions.choice: those who hate him ... him: each of them
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a plural, "those who hate", and goes on in the singular, "his face", "destroy him". Each one who hates God is dealt with in person.

decisions.choice: each one in person, them, that person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use English plurals and "each" where the Hebrew moves to the singular (m3). Literal keeps the singular, with "each one's" in brackets.

source.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֨ אֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֜ה וְאֶת־הַֽחֻקִּ֣ים וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ הַיּ֖וֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you shall keep the commandment and the statutes and the judgments which I [am] commanding you today, to do them.

en.L: So you shall keep the commandment and the statutes and the judgments which I am commanding you today, to do them.
en.B: So keep the commandment, the statutes and the rulings that I am giving you today, and carry them out.
en.R: So obey the command, the laws and the rules that I am giving you today. Do what they say.

decisions.choice: the commandment: the whole charge Moses gives
decisions.reason: The singular "commandment" sums up all that Moses teaches as one charge, the call to love and serve the LORD alone, with the statutes and judgments as its details (5:31; 6:1, 25).

decisions.choice: I am commanding you: Moses speaks
decisions.reason: "I" here is Moses, giving Israel the LORD's commands on the plains of Moab before they cross the Jordan (1:3-5; 5:1).

decisions.choice: commandment, statutes, judgments / rulings / rules
decisions.reason: The three words follow the terms used from Exodus to Deuteronomy: Literal "commandment, statutes, judgments", Balanced "statutes, rulings", Readable "command, laws, rules".

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀עֵ֣קֶב תִּשְׁמְע֗וּן אֵ֤ת הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְשָׁמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לְךָ֗ אֶֽת־הַבְּרִית֙ וְאֶת־הַחֶ֔סֶד אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לַאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, that will keep Yahweh your God for you the covenant and the steadfast love which he swore to your fathers.

en.L: And it will be, because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will keep for you the covenant and the steadfast love which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers.
en.B: If you listen to these rulings and keep them and carry them out, then in return {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will keep with you the covenant and the faithful love {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors on oath.
en.R: If you listen to these rules and obey them carefully, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with you. He will show you the faithful love {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors with an oath.

decisions.choice: because: as the result that follows on
decisions.reason: The word is the noun "heel", used to mean "as a consequence of": what follows on the heels of something (8:20; Genesis 22:18; 26:5). Israel's obedience and the LORD's keeping of his covenant go together.

decisions.choice: keep ... will keep: the same verb on both sides
decisions.reason: Israel is to keep the judgments, and the LORD will keep the covenant. The repeated verb shows the two sides of the bond. Moses speaks to the people in the plural here (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: the covenant and the steadfast love
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: God's loyal, faithful love that belongs to his covenant, promised to the patriarchs (verse 8).

decisions.choice: If ... then in return
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the link as a condition, since the blessing depends on listening and keeping; "in return" gives the sense of the Hebrew word (m1). Literal keeps "because".

decisions.choice: rulings, rules; ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verses 8 and 11.

source.text: וַאֲהֵ֣בְךָ֔ וּבֵרַכְךָ֖ וְהִרְבֶּ֑ךָ וּבֵרַ֣ךְ פְּרִֽי־בִטְנְךָ֣ וּפְרִֽי־אַ֠דְמָתֶךָ דְּגָ֨נְךָ֜ וְתִֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֗ךָ שְׁגַר־אֲלָפֶ֨יךָ֙ וְעַשְׁתְּרֹ֣ת צֹאנֶ֔ךָ עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ לָ֥תֶת לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will love you and bless you and multiply you, and he will bless [the] fruit of your womb and [the] fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, [the] offspring of your cattle and [the] young of your flock, on the ground which he swore to your fathers to give to you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will love you and bless you and multiply you; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock, on the ground which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers to give to you.
en.B: He will love you, bless you and make you numerous. He will bless the children you bear and the harvest of your soil, your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the young of your cattle and your sheep, in the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised on oath to your ancestors to give you.
en.R: He will love you, bless you and make your people grow in number. He will bless you with children and with good crops: grain, new wine and olive oil. He will bless you with calves in your herds and lambs in your flocks. All this will be in the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your ancestors with an oath to give you.

decisions.choice: fruit of your womb, fruit of your ground: your children and your crops
decisions.reason: "Fruit" is what grows from something: from the womb, children; from the ground, harvests. The blessings of 28:4 and 28:11 repeat the list.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and oil: the three main crops of the land
decisions.reason: Grain, fresh wine and fresh olive oil were the chief harvests of Canaan, often named together as the sign of a blessed land (11:14; 28:51; Hosea 2:10).

decisions.choice: offspring of your cattle, young of your flock: the increase of the herds
decisions.reason: Both are ordinary words here for the young born to cattle, sheep and goats (28:4, 18, 51; the first also in Exodus 13:12). The second is the same as the plural of Ashtoreth, the name of a Canaanite goddess (Judges 2:13; 1 Kings 11:5), and the first may also have been a god's name in the region. If the link was heard, the point is that the increase of the flocks comes from the LORD, not from the gods of the land.

decisions.choice: the children you bear, harvest; make you numerous
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the pictures mean (m1). Literal keeps "fruit of your womb", "fruit of your ground" and "multiply".

decisions.choice: the young of your cattle and your sheep; calves, lambs
decisions.reason: Balanced names the animals the young are born to, and Readable uses the plain words calves and lambs. Literal keeps "offspring" and "young".

source.text: בָּר֥וּךְ תִּֽהְיֶ֖ה מִכָּל־הָעַמִּ֑ים לֹא־יִהְיֶ֥ה בְךָ֛ עָקָ֥ר וַֽעֲקָרָ֖ה וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed you will be above all the peoples; not will be among you a barren male or a barren female, or among your livestock.

en.L: Blessed you shall be above all the peoples; there shall not be among you a barren male or a barren female, or among your livestock.
en.B: Of all peoples, you will be the most blessed. Among you there will be no man or woman unable to have children, and among your animals none that bears no young.
en.R: No nation will be as blessed as you. None of your men or women will be unable to have children. None of your animals will be unable to have young either.

decisions.choice: barren: unable to have children
decisions.reason: The words describe a man or a woman who cannot have children (Genesis 11:30; 25:21). The promise takes up Exodus 23:26 and reaches the livestock too.

decisions.choice: above all the peoples: more than any of them
decisions.reason: The preposition here compares: Israel will be blessed beyond every other people.

decisions.choice: unable to have children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "barren" means in plain words. Literal keeps "barren".

source.text: וְהֵסִ֧יר יְהוָ֛ה מִמְּךָ֖ כָּל־חֹ֑לִי וְכָל־מַדְוֵי֩ מִצְרַ֨יִם הָרָעִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֗עְתָּ לֹ֤א יְשִׂימָם֙ בָּ֔ךְ וּנְתָנָ֖ם בְּכָל־שֹׂנְאֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will turn away Yahweh from you all sickness, and all [the] diseases of Egypt, the evil ones, which you knew, not he will put them on you, and he will lay them on all those hating you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will turn away from you every sickness; and all the evil diseases of Egypt which you knew, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not put them on you, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lay them on all who hate you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep every sickness away from you. None of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you came to know will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bring on you; instead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will put them on all who hate you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep all sickness away from you. You know about the terrible diseases in Egypt. He will not let them come on you. Instead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will put them on everyone who hates you.

decisions.choice: the diseases of Egypt: illnesses Israel saw there
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the LORD's promise after the crossing of the sea: "none of the diseases I put on Egypt will I put on you" (Exodus 15:26). It may point to the plagues, such as the boils (Exodus 9:9-11), or to illnesses known in Egypt; 28:27 and 28:60 turn the same threat against a disobedient Israel.

decisions.choice: which you knew: which you saw for yourselves
decisions.reason: To "know" here means to have experience of something, to have seen it at first hand.

decisions.choice: all who hate you: Israel's enemies
decisions.reason: Those who hate Israel are its enemies; the curse they would wish on Israel falls on them instead (30:7).

decisions.choice: dreadful, terrible
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls the diseases "evil", meaning harmful. Balanced says "dreadful" and Readable "terrible"; Literal keeps "evil".

source.text: וְאָכַלְתָּ֣ אֶת־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ לֹא־תָחֹ֥ס עֵֽינְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹ֤א תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־מוֹקֵ֥שׁ ה֖וּא לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you shall devour all the peoples which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you; not shall pity your eye on them, and not you shall serve their gods, for a snare it [is] to you.

en.L: And you shall devour all the peoples which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you; your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not serve their gods, for that [would be] a snare to you.
en.B: You are to make an end of all the peoples {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is handing over to you. Let no pity for them hold you back, and do not serve their gods; that would be a trap to catch you.
en.R: You must destroy all the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is letting you defeat. Do not feel sorry for them. And do not worship their gods, because that would trap you.

decisions.choice: devour: destroy completely
decisions.reason: The verb is "eat". Used of enemies, it means to consume them entirely, as fire eats up what it burns (Numbers 14:9; Jeremiah 10:25).

decisions.choice: your eye shall not pity: let no pity hold you back
decisions.reason: The eye shows what the heart feels. The phrase forbids sparing someone out of pity (13:9; 19:13, 21; 25:12). It repeats the command of verse 2.

decisions.choice: snare: a trap that lures and catches
decisions.reason: A snare is a bird trap. As in Exodus 23:33 and 34:12, serving the gods of the land would catch Israel and destroy it. "That" most likely refers to serving their gods, or to the peoples left alive.

decisions.choice: make an end of, destroy; trap
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "devour" means (m1); "trap" is the plain word for a snare. Literal keeps "devour" and "snare".

source.text: כִּ֤י תֹאמַר֙ בִּלְבָ֣בְךָ֔ רַבִּ֛ים הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִמֶּ֑נִּי אֵיכָ֥ה אוּכַ֖ל לְהוֹרִישָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: If you say in your heart, many [are] the nations these more than I; how can I dispossess them?

en.L: If you say in your heart, 'These nations [are] more numerous than I; how can I dispossess them?'
en.B: Perhaps you will think to yourself, 'These nations outnumber us. How could we ever drive them out?'
en.R: Maybe you will think, 'There are many more of them than of us. How can we ever force them out?'

decisions.choice: say in your heart: think to yourself
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and decides. To say something in the heart is to think it without speaking (8:17; 9:4).

decisions.choice: dispossess: drive out and take the place of
decisions.reason: The verb used for taking possession of the land (verse 1) here has the nations as its object: to drive them out so that their land passes to Israel (9:1; 11:23).

decisions.choice: if: the fear Moses foresees
decisions.reason: The word can mean "if" or "when". Moses names a fear Israel may feel, and answers it in verses 18-24, as he did after the spies' report (1:28-30).

decisions.choice: us, we
decisions.reason: Israel speaks as one person, "I", as the nation is addressed as "you" (verse 1). Balanced and Readable use "we", since English does not speak of a nation as "I". Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: לֹ֥א תִירָ֖א מֵהֶ֑ם זָכֹ֣ר תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לְפַרְעֹ֖ה וּלְכָל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall be afraid of them; remembering you shall remember what did Yahweh your God to Pharaoh and to all Egypt,

en.L: You shall not be afraid of them; you shall surely remember what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt,
en.B: Do not fear them. Keep firmly in mind what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Pharaoh and the whole of Egypt,
en.R: Do not be afraid of them. Instead, remember clearly what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Pharaoh and to the whole land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: you shall surely remember: an emphatic command
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. To remember in Deuteronomy is not only to recall but to let what God has done shape how one lives (5:15; 8:2; 15:15). Memory of the exodus is the answer to fear.

decisions.choice: what the LORD did: spelled out in verse 19
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on: verse 19 lists what the LORD did to Egypt and draws the lesson.

decisions.choice: the whole land of Egypt
decisions.reason: "All Egypt" means the land and its people; Readable says so. Readable also ends the sentence here and begins verse 19 afresh.

source.text: הַמַּסֹּ֨ת הַגְּדֹלֹ֜ת אֲשֶׁר־רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ וְהָאֹתֹ֤ת וְהַמֹּֽפְתִים֙ וְהַיָּ֤ד הַחֲזָקָה֙ וְהַזְּרֹ֣עַ הַנְּטוּיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כֵּֽן־יַעֲשֶׂ֞ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לְכָל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה יָרֵ֖א מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: the trials great which saw your eyes, and the signs and the wonders and the hand the strong and the arm the outstretched, by which brought you out Yahweh your God; so will do Yahweh your God to all the peoples whom you [are] afraid of [their] face.

en.L: the great trials which your eyes saw, and the signs and the wonders, and the strong hand and the outstretched arm, by which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out. So will {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid.
en.B: the great trials that you watched with your own eyes, the signs, the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm by which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God led you out. That is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will do to every people you are afraid of.
en.R: You saw with your own eyes the great troubles {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought on them. You saw the signs and wonders. You saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power at work when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought you out of Egypt. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will do the same to all the nations you are afraid of.

decisions.choice: trials: tests that proved who God is
decisions.reason: The word means a testing or trial. Here it refers to the plagues on Egypt, which put Pharaoh to the test and showed the power of the LORD (4:34; 29:2).

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues and the rescue from Egypt
decisions.reason: Signs point beyond themselves to God; wonders are deeds beyond the ordinary. The pair names the events of the exodus (Exodus 7:3; Deuteronomy 4:34; 6:22).

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: An arm stretched out is ready to strike. Together the two pictures describe God's mighty acts for Israel (4:34; 5:15; 26:8).

decisions.choice: the great troubles he brought on them; his great power at work; out of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable makes separate sentences and says what the trials and the hand and arm were. It names Egypt, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

source.text: וְגַם֙ אֶת־הַצִּרְעָ֔ה יְשַׁלַּ֛ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בָּ֑ם עַד־אֲבֹ֗ד הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֛ים וְהַנִּסְתָּרִ֖ים מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the hornet will send Yahweh your God among them, until perish those remaining and those hiding from your face.

en.L: And also the hornet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will send among them, until those who are left and those who hide themselves from you perish.
en.B: What is more, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will send the hornet against them, until even those left alive and in hiding from you are gone.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will also send hornets among them. Even those who escape and hide from you will die.

decisions.choice: the hornet: the meaning of the word is uncertain
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 23:28, where the word first appears; it is also found in Joshua 24:12. It is usually taken as "hornet", a stinging insect, whether real or a picture of a terror that drives people to flight. Some take it as "discouragement" or "plague". The point is clear either way: God himself drives the enemy out.

decisions.choice: those who are left and those who hide: survivors who escape the fighting
decisions.reason: Even those who survive the battle and hide from Israel will not escape. The verb "perish" means to come to an end.

decisions.choice: hornets
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, as in Exodus 23:28, since the Hebrew singular names the kind of creature.

source.text: לֹ֥א תַעֲרֹ֖ץ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בְּקִרְבֶּ֔ךָ אֵ֥ל גָּד֖וֹל וְנוֹרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you shall dread from their faces, for Yahweh your God [is] in your midst, a God great and awesome.

en.L: You shall not dread them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] in your midst, a great and awe-inspiring God.
en.B: Do not tremble before them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is there among you, a God great and awe-inspiring.
en.R: Do not be terrified of them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is right there with you. He is great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fills people with awe.

decisions.choice: dread: tremble in fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake with terror. Moses used it when Israel refused to go into the land (1:29), and it returns before battle (20:3; 31:6).

decisions.choice: in your midst: the LORD present among his people
decisions.reason: God is not far off; he goes with Israel and is present in the camp (6:15; 23:15; Numbers 14:14). That is the reason Israel need not fear.

decisions.choice: awe-inspiring: one who is to be feared
decisions.reason: The word means one who causes fear and reverent awe (10:17, 21; Exodus 15:11). The fear that Israel feels for the nations belongs rightly to God.

decisions.choice: awe-inspiring; fills people with awe
decisions.reason: "Awesome" is now often a casual word of praise in English, so all levels say "awe-inspiring" or put it in a plain clause.

source.text: וְנָשַׁל֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֛ל מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ מְעַ֣ט מְעָ֑ט לֹ֤א תוּכַל֙ כַּלֹּתָ֣ם מַהֵ֔ר פֶּן־תִּרְבֶּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will clear away Yahweh your God the nations these from before you little little; not you will be able to finish them quickly, lest will multiply against you [the] beast[s] of the field.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will clear away these nations before you little by little; you will not be able to make an end of them quickly, lest the animals of the field become too many for you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will clear these nations out of your way a little at a time. You will not be able to finish them off all at once, or the wild animals would become too many for you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will force these nations out a little at a time. You will not be able to destroy them all at once. If you did, wild animals would become too many for you.

decisions.choice: little by little: a little at a time
decisions.reason: The word "little" is doubled, as in Exodus 23:29-30, where God gave the same plan and the same reason.

decisions.choice: you will not be able: the LORD sets the pace
decisions.reason: The verb means "be able", and can carry the sense "may not". Either way, the land is not emptied in one stroke; God gives it over as Israel can fill it (Exodus 23:30). Verses 23-24 speak of the full victory at the end of that process.

decisions.choice: the animals of the field: wild beasts
decisions.reason: A land left empty of people soon becomes a home for wild animals such as lions (Exodus 23:29; 2 Kings 17:25-26).

decisions.choice: wild animals
decisions.reason: "The animals of the field" means wild animals, as opposed to livestock; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

source.text: וּנְתָנָ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְהָמָם֙ מְהוּמָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד הִשָּׁמְדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will give them Yahweh your God before you, and will throw them into confusion great until they are destroyed.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give them [over] before you, and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will hand them over to you and throw them into great panic until they are wiped out.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will let you defeat them. He will fill them with panic until they are destroyed.

decisions.choice: great confusion: panic sent by God
decisions.reason: The noun and its verb are used of God throwing an enemy into panic before battle (Exodus 23:27; Joshua 10:10; 1 Samuel 5:9, 11). The same word is a curse on a disobedient Israel in 28:20.

decisions.choice: give them before you: hand them over
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: panic
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "panic", the sense of the word in battle; Literal keeps "confusion".

source.text: וְנָתַ֤ן מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְהַאֲבַדְתָּ֣ אֶת־שְׁמָ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם לֹֽא־יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב אִישׁ֙ בְּפָנֶ֔יךָ עַ֥ד הִשְׁמִֽדְךָ֖ אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will give their kings into your hand, and you shall make perish their name from under the heavens; not will stand a man before you until you have destroyed them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give their kings into your hand, and you shall make their name perish from under the heavens; no one shall stand before you until you have destroyed them.
en.B: He will put their kings in your power, and you will blot their name out from under heaven. No one will hold out against you until you have destroyed them.
en.R: He will let you defeat their kings. You will destroy them so completely that no one under heaven will remember their names. No one will be able to stop you until you have destroyed them.

decisions.choice: into your hand: into your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (1:27; 2:24; 3:2).

decisions.choice: make their name perish from under heaven: wipe out every memory of them
decisions.reason: A name is how a person or line is remembered. To make it perish "from under heaven" is to end it on the whole earth (9:14; 25:19; 29:19). It may mean the kings' names or the peoples' name; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: stand before you: hold one's ground against you
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's stand. No one will be able to resist Israel (11:25; Joshua 1:5).

decisions.choice: so completely that no one ... will remember their names
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of a name perishing means (m2).

source.text: פְּסִילֵ֥י אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם תִּשְׂרְפ֣וּן בָּאֵ֑שׁ לֹֽא־תַחְמֹד֩ כֶּ֨סֶף וְזָהָ֤ב עֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ לָ֔ךְ פֶּ֚ן תִּוָּקֵ֣שׁ בּ֔וֹ כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: The carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire; not you shall covet [the] silver and gold on them and take [it] for yourself, lest you be snared by it, for an abomination of Yahweh your God it [is].

en.L: The carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver and the gold on them and take [it] for yourself, lest you be snared by it, for it [is] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.B: Burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. Do not set your heart on the silver or gold that covers them, and do not carry it off for yourself; it would catch you like a trap, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God detests it.
en.R: Burn the idols of their gods. Do not want the silver or gold on them, and do not keep it for yourself. If you do, it will trap you. It is disgusting to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: covet: desire to have for oneself
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the last commandment (5:21). Achan later took what was devoted and said, "I coveted them and took them" (Joshua 7:21), the very pair of verbs used here.

decisions.choice: silver and gold on them: the metal covering of idols
decisions.reason: Images of wood or stone were often plated with silver or gold (Isaiah 30:22; 40:19). The metal belonged to the idol and was to be destroyed with it, not kept as plunder.

decisions.choice: an abomination: something the LORD detests
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 18:22: what God finds abhorrent and will not accept. In Deuteronomy the word is used above all for the gods and worship of the nations (12:31; 13:15; 18:9-12).

decisions.choice: be snared: be caught as in a trap
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with the "snare" of verse 16. Keeping the precious metal would draw Israel toward the idol it came from.

decisions.choice: the LORD your God detests it (Balanced); disgusting (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 18:22, where Balanced says "detestable"; here the verb reads more naturally. Literal keeps "abomination".

source.text: וְלֹא־תָבִ֤יא תֽוֹעֵבָה֙ אֶל־בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ חֵ֖רֶם כָּמֹ֑הוּ שַׁקֵּ֧ץ׀תְּשַׁקְּצֶ֛נּוּ וְתַעֵ֥ב׀תְּֽתַעֲבֶ֖נּוּ כִּי־חֵ֥רֶם הֽוּא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not you shall bring an abomination into your house, and you will be a devoted thing like it; detesting you shall detest it and abhorring you shall abhor it, for a devoted thing it [is].

en.L: And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and become a devoted thing like it; you shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it [is] a devoted thing.
en.B: Do not bring anything detestable into your home; if you do, you will become a devoted thing just as it is, marked for destruction. Loathe it and detest it with all your being, for it is a devoted thing.
en.R: Do not bring any such disgusting thing into your home, or you will be doomed to destruction along with it. Hate it and reject it completely, because it must be destroyed, given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a devoted thing: something under the ban, given over to destruction
decisions.reason: The noun belongs with the verb of verse 2. An idol and its metal are devoted things: they belong to the LORD only by being destroyed. Whoever takes such a thing into his house comes under the same ban and shares its fate (13:18; Joshua 6:18; 7:1, 11-12, 24-26).

decisions.choice: utterly detest ... utterly abhor: the strongest rejection
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis. The first is used for unclean creatures that must not be eaten (Leviticus 11:11-13); the second is the verb of "abomination" in verse 25.

decisions.choice: and become: what would follow
decisions.reason: The clause says what would happen if the forbidden thing were brought in: the household would become devoted with it.

decisions.choice: marked for destruction
decisions.reason: Balanced adds what being a devoted thing means here, as Leviticus 27:29 does, since "devoted" alone can sound like loyalty.

decisions.choice: doomed to destruction along with it; it must be destroyed, given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the noun in plain words, as the verb is explained in verse 2. Literal and Balanced keep "devoted thing".
